weakness.title: Unreliable Timestamps on Access Events
weakness.description: Access events carry timestamps that are inaccurate, inconsistent between devices or modifiable, so events cannot be ordered or matched with other records.

extended_description.applicability: Readers, controllers, recorders, cameras, alarm panels and servers that stamp events with a time. Includes devices that keep their own clock without synchronization, clocks that can be set by users, and mixed time zones or daylight saving rules.
extended_description.exploitation: An access cannot be placed in time with confidence, so it cannot be matched to other events or disproved, and an alibi or a false accusation cannot be tested.

row.details: Records from different sources cannot be aligned to reconstruct an incident.
Times of access can be disputed, which weakens attribution.
Time-based rules and correlations produce false results or miss events.

row.description: Set every device from a single trusted time source and monitor the offset.
Allow only named administrators to change the time of a device, and record each change.
Record time in a single reference, such as UTC, with the time zone stated.
Compare timestamps across devices on a schedule and alert when the difference exceeds a set limit.

row.measure: Retain the time source of each event
row.description: Keep the source of the timestamp to tell device time from server time.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-8 Time Stamps
